title: Write a PersistentVolumeClaim
intro: tutorial-011 taught get/describe for existing PVCs. Writing one from scratch means getting the storage request's quantity syntax and access mode right.

steps.prompt: Write a PersistentVolumeClaim named 'db-data' requesting 10Gi of storage with ReadWriteOnce access, using the 'standard' storage class.
steps.hint: accessModes is a list even though you're only specifying one value. resources.requests.storage uses the same quantity format as CPU/memory (a number plus a unit, like '10Gi').
steps.solution:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: db-data
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
  storageClassName: standard
steps.explanation: Once this PVC exists and binds to a matching PersistentVolume (or one gets dynamically provisioned by the 'standard' StorageClass), a pod can reference it by name in spec.volumes — the pod spec itself never needs to know which actual disk is behind it.
steps.why: accessModes being a list, not a single string, is the detail people most often get wrong from memory — it's plural because some volume types genuinely support being claimed with more than one mode at once (e.g. ReadWriteOnce and ReadOnlyMany together), even though a single mode is the common case.
